title: The Lunch at Chickenland That Turned Into Nando's
conflicts: Price: about US$100,000 (The Edge, 2009) vs about 80,000 rand (Wikipedia citing Fick 2002); too far apart, so no price is given. Stake: 67% first, outright in 1990 (Wikipedia citing an HBS interview that is blocked); story says only that they bought the building and business, per the heritage plaque. Name: could not register Fernando's, chose Nando's, also his son's name (Brozin 2009) vs named after Duarte's first-born son (plaque) vs after Fernando, known as Nando (Khaleej Times); Brozin's account used. Ambition: 'take it global' (Brozin 2009 recollection) vs 'no real plans for immediate expansion' (2004 release); noted.
notes: Several Ptahhotep maxims are already used elsewhere (the accounts/heart line was the first choice but is taken); maxim 33 on knowing a friend is new. Outlet count (700 in 26 countries) is the 2009 figure and is dated in the story. Quote stance: affirms.
